muxt generate --use-receiver-type=T
muxt check

exec go test -count=1

-- template.gohtml --
{{- define "GET /api/user 201 marshalJSON(GetUser(ctx))" -}}{{- end -}}
-- go.mod --
module server

go 1.24
-- template.go --
package server

import (
	"context"
	"embed"
	"html/template"
)

//go:embed *.gohtml
var templatesFS embed.FS

var templates = template.Must(template.ParseFS(templatesFS, "*"))

type User struct {
	Name string   `json:"name"`
	Age  int      `json:"age"`
	Tags []string `json:"tags"`
}

type T struct{}

// GetUser returns a struct with a nil slice: encoding/json (v1) renders it as
// null, which the jsonv2 sibling archive contrasts with [].
func (T) GetUser(_ context.Context) (User, error) {
	return User{Name: "Ada", Age: 36}, nil
}
-- template_test.go --
package server

import (
	"net/http"
	"net/http/httptest"
	"testing"
)

func Test(t *testing.T) {
	mux := http.NewServeMux()
	TemplateRoutes(mux, T{})

	req := httptest.NewRequest(http.MethodGet, "/api/user", nil)
	rec := httptest.NewRecorder()
	mux.ServeHTTP(rec, req)

	if rec.Code != http.StatusCreated {
		t.Errorf("status = %d, want %d (the route's declared status code)", rec.Code, http.StatusCreated)
	}
	if got, want := rec.Header().Get("Content-Type"), "application/json"; got != want {
		t.Errorf("Content-Type = %q, want %q", got, want)
	}
	if want := `{"name":"Ada","age":36,"tags":null}`; rec.Body.String() != want {
		t.Errorf("body = %q, want %q", rec.Body.String(), want)
	}
}
